summary: Credential chaining failure when assuming cross-account roles; intermittent AWS STS and GCP SA impersonation errors
description:
Issue summary:
Customers and internal tooling intermittently fail to assume newly provisioned cross-account roles or impersonate GCP service accounts using the standard ephemeral access flow. Errors started appearing after a configuration change to org-level guardrails last week. Impact: SRE and infra automation jobs intermittently fail (30-60s spikes) when chaining AssumeRole/impersonation across accounts, causing deployments and scheduled reconciliations to retry and sometimes miss windows.

Impact:
- Internal deploy pipelines (infra-reconciler) experienced multiple retries during routine rollout windows.
- On-call engineers had to perform manual escalation for time-sensitive hotfixes.

Environment:
- AWS production account family with cross-account IAM roles (redwood-core -> dedicated-ops)
- GCP production org with service-account impersonation via workload identity and short-lived tokens

Request:
- Identify why sts:AssumeRole and iam.serviceAccounts.get / iam.serviceAccounts.implicitDelegation calls fail intermittently for ephemeral sessions and restore stable chaining behavior.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a new ephemeral key session using vault-jit to assume arn:aws:iam::DEST:role/infra-debug-role from operator account.
2) Run infra-reconciler job that performs cross-account SSM/API calls.
3) Observe transient AssumeRole/AccessDenied errors; repeat until failure reproduces.
4) On GCP side, request short-lived token via iamcredentials.servicesAccounts.generateAccessToken impersonating project-prod-sa and observe 403 or 'serviceAccounts.get failed' in about 1 of 8 requests.
observed_behavior:
AWS: 'AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole on resource arn:aws:iam::DEST:role/infra-debug-role' appears intermittently. Sometimes we see 'InvalidIdentityToken' immediately after a successful vault token exchange.
GCP: 'Permission denied: Service account project-prod-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com does not exist or caller lacks iam.serviceAccounts.get' intermittently. Logs show brief windows where the service account is unresolvable from impersonation endpoint.
expected_behavior: Ephemeral sessions should be able to assume cross-account roles and impersonate service accounts reliably. No intermittent AccessDenied or 'service account not found' errors during normal operations.
logs:
AWS CloudTrail snippets:
- 2026-03-09T21:14:03Z sts:AssumeRole CallerArn: arn:aws:sts::OPR:assumed-role/jit-broker/xxx -> Error: AccessDenied
- 2026-03-09T21:14:03Z iam:PassRole allowed for role but AssumeRole denied with policy evaluation: 'explicit deny from org SCP' seen in evaluation context.
GCP AuditLog:
- 2026-03-10T02:05:12Z iamcredentials.generateAccessToken proto: PERMISSION_DENIED for serviceAccount: project-prod-sa
- 2026-03-10T02:05:12Z preceding logs show policy binding updates to folder guardrail managed by security-team.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypotheses:
- Org-level guardrail/SCP introduced last week contains a conditional deny that sometimes applies when the request context lacks a specific tag/attribute for ephemeral sessions. The deny appears to be flaky due to timing of tag propagation or evaluation order between accounts.
- On AWS: There is a permission boundary applied to the intermediate role (jit-broker) that prevents it from assuming certain target roles if session tags are present/absent.
- On GCP: Workload Identity config may be missing the 'iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator' binding for the impersonating identity in some projects, and folder-level IAM binding changes may not have propagated fully to all nodes causing intermittent 403s.
- Network/DNS unlikely; errors are permission-eval related per CloudTrail and Audit logs.

What we've done so far:
- Replayed the vault-jit assume flow in staging; reproduced AssumeRole failure when session tags included 'requester:automation'.
- Rolled back the most recent folder-level IAM change in a test org; impersonation success rate in test jumped from 88% to 100% during a 2-hour window.
- Correlated failures with recent org-SCPs rolled out by security on 2026-03-08.

Next steps proposed:
- Ask Security to review the SCP / folder deny conditions (trace: GH PR #infra/guardrails/relax-20260308).
- Temporarily adjust permission boundary and test assume flow to isolate boundary vs SCP behavior.
- Add metrics to vault-jit and infra-reconciler to emit full policy evaluation ARNs for failed assume calls for faster triage.
- If root cause confirmed as SCP timing/conditional evaluation, coordinate a safe rollback-window and add a canary policy to prevent denial for ephemeral sessions.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:18 - Aisha Patel: Noticed spike in infra-reconciler failures during deploy window; opened this ticket to coordinate with Security and IAM owners.
2026-03-10 10:03 - Miguel Ortega: Assigned. Will attempt to reproduce in staging and capture full policy evaluation JSON from CloudTrail + org SCP logs.
2026-03-10 13:45 - SRE Oncall (Lena Kim): We saw retries causing backoff storms; temp workaround was to force jobs to use long-lived role for critical hotfixes. Need proper fix to avoid manual steps.

2026-03-11 08:22 - Security (Tomás Alvarez): We're reviewing the SCP changes from 2026-03-08. We suspect a condition on aws:PrincipalTag missing for JIT sessions is causing an implicit deny. Will prepare a narrow exception for ephemeral sessions.

2026-03-11 15:40 - Miguel Ortega: Reproduced locally: when session tag 'requester' is present, permission boundary evaluation blocks AssumeRole into infra-debug-role. Removing the tag allows assume to succeed. Pushing a test PR to adjust vault-jit tagging behavior.

2026-03-12 11:12 - Miguel Ortega: Coordinated with Tomas; Security applied a scoped exception in the SCP to allow sts:AssumeRole when sessionContext includes tag 'xref:ephemeral' AND caller is member of 'infra-jit' OU. Monitoring for 24h.
2026-03-12 16:28 - Lena Kim: Post-change, retry rate for infra-reconciler dropped from 22% to 2% in us-east. GCP impersonation errors also fell but still see rare 403s (~0.5%).
resolution:
Temporary scoped exception to org SCP applied to allow ephemeral sessions tagged with 'xref:ephemeral' to perform sts:AssumeRole; vault-jit modified to include the tag on ephemeral sessions with a follow-up PR merged. On GCP, Security added a narrow iam.serviceAccounts.get binding for the impersonating principal in affected projects while investigating folder-level propagation. Monitoring agreed for 72 hours.

Follow-ups:
- Security to propose an automated test for future SCP changes to prevent accidental denies for ephemeral flows.
- Miguel to add policy-eval instrumentation to vault-jit and infra-reconciler (ticket created).
- Closure will be conditional on 72h stability period and postmortem doc.
